# Audition-to-Invoice Business Tracker for Freelance Voice Actors and Audiobook Narrators

*Generated by Forge on 2026-05-04T01:48:23.985Z — score 8.2/10*

## Overview

**NarraTrack** (slug: `audition-invoice-tracker-voice-actors-narrators`) is a web SaaS dashboard built for freelance voice actors and ACX audiobook narrators who manage their business through a tangle of spreadsheets, notes apps, and generic CRMs. The product replaces that patchwork with a single pipeline: log an audition, track its status, record a booking, capture the rights type (buyout vs. royalty-share), project royalty-share ROI over time, generate an invoice, and log payment — all with ACX-specific terminology and logic baked in from day one. It is a Next.js web app deployed to Coolify, designed to be fast on a laptop and readable on a phone, with no native mobile build required.

---

## Why this will succeed

### Comparable products that are working

**Bonsai** (hellobonsai.com) — estimated ~$50M ARR, 500K+ freelancer users. Works because it wraps contract-to-invoice workflow into one product for a specific freelancer audience (web designers, consultants). The model of "purpose-built SaaS for a freelancer type" is proven at scale. Its failure mode for narrators is structural: the entire product assumes B2B client relationships, not platform-mediated marketplace transactions like ACX. There is no concept of a per-finished-hour (PFH) rate, an exclusivity window, a royalty-share split, or an audition pipeline.

**Dubsado** (dubsado.com) — estimated ~$10M ARR, popular among photographers and creative service providers. Works because it solves end-to-end client workflow for a vertical that was previously spreadsheet-dependent. Same structural problem for narrators: built around proposals, onboarding questionnaires, and client portals. ACX narrators do not onboard clients — they submit auditions to a marketplace and wait. The vocabulary is wrong at every screen.

**HoneyBook** (honeybook.com) — estimated ~$100M ARR, primarily photographers and event planners. Works because it serves a passionate, community-driven creative professional audience who refer each other inside tight Facebook and Instagram communities — which is exactly the distribution model available here. Its weakness for narrators is pure overkill: the product is built around proposals, signed contracts, and client portals. A narrator tracking 50 ACX auditions per month needs none of that.

**The pattern:** purpose-built freelancer workflow SaaS consistently reaches $10–100M ARR. The comparable tools prove the price point ($20–40/mo), the distribution model (community-first), and the willingness to pay. None of them serve ACX narrators specifically.

### Specific data points from research

- The **ACX narrator Facebook group has 30,000+ members** with **spreadsheet templates pinned in the community posts** as the de facto solution. A pinned spreadsheet template is not an abstract market signal — it is proof that (a) the problem is real, (b) no adequate product exists, and (c) the community has already self-organized around a workaround that a product can replace.
- **ACX has approximately 50,000 registered narrators**; the estimated active working narrators submitting auditions regularly are 8,000–15,000. The addressable paid target — narrators treating this as primary income — is ~2,000. At $19/mo, that is a $38,000/mo TAM ceiling for the core segment alone.
- Keywords like **"acx narrator royalty share calculator"** and **"voice actor audition tracking software"** are described in the research as low-competition, high-intent long-tail queries that a solo dev can realistically rank for within 3 months. No dedicated tool currently occupies these SERPs.
- **r/VoiceActing** (~90K members) provides a secondary organic seeding channel with demonstrated audience activity around freelance VO business questions.
- Two independent research signals (ProductHunt and search autocomplete) surfaced this gap — a meaningful cross-signal that the demand is real and already being expressed.

### Why this specific opportunity is different

The three comparable tools fail narrators not because of missing features — they fail because their **data model is wrong**. None of them have a concept of a royalty-share split, a per-finished-hour rate, an ACX exclusivity window, or an audition submission state machine. Building those concepts natively means the product is not "Bonsai but for narrators" — it is the first tool that speaks the narrator's actual language. The 30K-member Facebook group running on pinned spreadsheets is the clearest possible signal that no one has built this yet.

## Target user

**Primary persona: The Working ACX Narrator**

Sarah is 34, based in the US Midwest, and treats audiobook narration as her primary income stream — she earns $3,000–$6,000/month from a mix of ACX buyout titles and royalty-share projects. She submits 15–30 auditions per month and manages a portfolio of 40+ active titles. She tracks everything in a Google Sheet she built herself from a template she found pinned in the ACX narrator Facebook group. The sheet has six tabs, three of which are out of date, and she cannot quickly answer "how much am I making per finished hour across all my royalty-share titles this quarter."

She currently fails to track: audition-to-booking conversion rate, exclusivity window expiry dates for titles she might want to renegotiate, projected cumulative royalties on individual titles, and total payment outstanding across all books. She uses PayPal invoicing for direct clients and tracks ACX payments manually.

She hangs out online in the ACX narrator Facebook group (daily), r/VoiceActing (weekly), and listens to 2–3 VO business podcasts. She is willing to pay $20–30/month for a tool that demonstrably saves her time and money — she pays Bonsai or similar for other freelance admin but finds it useless for her ACX-specific workflow.

## Core features (MVP)

**Audition Pipeline**
- Add audition: title, author, word count/finished hours, client/publisher, submission date, audition status (submitted / awaiting response / booked / passed / expired)
- Status change triggers notification (email via Resend) when manually updated
- Audition list view with filters: status, date range, rights type
- Conversion rate dashboard widget: auditions submitted → booked (rolling 30/90 days)

**Booking & Project Tracker**
- Convert audition to booking in one click
- Booking fields: title, rights type (buyout / royalty-share / union residual), agreed rate (flat fee or PFH), finished hours logged, exclusivity window start/end date, delivery deadline
- Project status: in production / delivered / payment pending / paid / dispute

**Royalty-Share ROI Calculator**
- Per-title input: finished hours, agreed royalty split (%), ACX retail price, estimated monthly sales volume (narrator's own estimate)
- Output: breakeven month (when cumulative royalties exceed what a buyout would have paid at market PFH rate), 12-month projected earnings, 24-month projected earnings
- Comparison view: side-by-side royalty-share vs. buyout equivalent across all active royalty-share titles

**Rate History & Benchmarking**
- Log every rate offered and accepted per client/project type
- PFH rate history chart over time (simple line chart via Recharts)
- Manual benchmark input ("ACX average buyout: $X PFH") for comparison line on chart

**Invoice & Payment Tracker**
- Create invoice: client, project, amount, due date, payment terms
- Invoice status: draft / sent / paid / overdue
- Payment log: amount received, date, payment method (ACX direct / PayPal / check)
- Outstanding balance dashboard widget: total invoiced vs. total received

**Dashboard**
- Summary widgets: active auditions, conversion rate (30-day), total outstanding, MRR equivalent from royalty-share titles, next exclusivity window expiry
- No charts needed beyond the rate history line chart — tables + numbers are the MVP

**Auth & Account**
- Email/password signup + Google OAuth via NextAuth v5
- Single-user account (no team features in MVP)
- Data export: CSV export of auditions, bookings, and payment history

## Tech stack recommendation

**Standard stack — no deviations required.**

- **Next.js 15 (App Router) + TypeScript** — dashboard-heavy with server components for table data fetching, client components for form interactions
- **PostgreSQL + Prisma ORM** — relational data model fits the audition → booking → invoice → payment pipeline naturally; foreign keys enforce referential integrity
- **Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui** — Table, Dialog, Select, DatePicker, Badge components cover 90% of the UI; no custom component library needed
- **NextAuth v5 with Google OAuth + Prisma adapter** — auth required from day one; email/password + Google OAuth covers the audience
- **Stripe** — subscription billing at $19/mo (Starter) and $29/mo (Pro); yearly plan at $149 handled via Stripe's billing portal
- **Resend** — transactional email: welcome, booking status change, overdue invoice reminder, exclusivity window expiry alert (7-day warning)
- **Recharts** — rate history line chart (lightweight, works with React server/client boundary)
- **Coolify (Docker, `output: standalone`)** — standard deployment target

No mobile framework. The product is a data-dense dashboard; responsive Tailwind layout covers mobile-web adequately for the use cases (checking a booking status, logging a payment) without native app overhead.

## Monetization & pricing

**Primary strategy: subscription with a free trial, no permanent free tier.**

| Tier | Price | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| **Starter** | $19/mo or $149/yr | Audition pipeline (unlimited), booking tracker, invoice tracker, payment log, CSV export, dashboard |
| **Pro** | $29/mo or $229/yr | Everything in Starter + royalty-share ROI calculator, rate history benchmarking, exclusivity window alerts via email, priority support |

**Rationale:** Bonsai charges $25/mo and Dubsado charges $20/mo for generic freelancer tools that don't serve narrators at all. A purpose-built tool with ACX-specific features justifies the same floor — there is no competitive pressure to undercut. The royalty-share ROI calculator is the highest-value feature (it directly models earnings decisions worth thousands of dollars per title) and is the correct Pro gate because narrators with a large royalty-share portfolio are the highest-willingness-to-pay segment.

**14-day free trial** on all plans — no credit card required. This removes signup friction from the community seeding play; narrators can evaluate the tool before committing. Free trial converts to paid at Stripe checkout on day 14 (reminder email at day 10 via Resend).

**No permanent free tier.** A freemium model with limited auditions or projects creates support overhead and dilutes the community seeding play (the goal is paying users, not a large free user base).

## Competitor landscape

**Bonsai** (hellobonsai.com)
- Pricing: $25/mo (Starter), $39/mo (Professional), $79/mo (Business)
- Key features: contracts, proposals, invoicing, time tracking, client portal, expense tracking
- Gap/weakness: zero ACX-specific data model. No concept of royalty-share split, PFH rate, audition pipeline, or exclusivity window. A narrator using Bonsai still maintains a separate spreadsheet for the ACX-specific data layer. UI terminology (clients, projects, proposals) is alien to a marketplace-based workflow.
- Our differentiation: we are purpose-built for the ACX/VO workflow — audition states, royalty-share ROI modeling, PFH rate history, and exclusivity window tracking are first-class features, not bolt-ons.

**Dubsado** (dubsado.com)
- Pricing: $20/mo or $200/yr
- Key features: client onboarding workflows, questionnaires, contracts, invoicing, scheduler, client portal
- Gap/weakness: the entire product architecture assumes a B2B client relationship. ACX narrators transact through a marketplace, not direct client relationships. Dubsado's workflow automation (onboarding questionnaires, proposal templates) has no applicability. Narrators who try it report needing a parallel spreadsheet for audition tracking anyway.
- Our differentiation: we eliminate the parallel spreadsheet entirely by modeling the ACX submission-to-payment pipeline natively.

**HoneyBook** (honeybook.com)
- Pricing: $19/mo (Starter), $39/mo (Essentials), $79/mo (Premium)
- Key features: inquiry forms, proposals, contracts, payments, project management, client experience tools
- Gap/weakness: built for photographers and event planners with in-person client relationships. No royalty or residuals modeling, no audition submission states. Overkill for a narrator's workflow in every direction that matters; missing in every direction that does.
- Our differentiation: narrower, deeper — we do less overall but solve the actual problem completely.

**No dedicated VO/narrator business tracker exists.** The research confirms this explicitly — the ACX narrator community's de facto solution is a pinned spreadsheet template. This is not a market with a dominant incumbent to displace; it is a market with a vacuum.

## Build instructions for the coding agent

1. **Initialize the project:**
   ```
   npx create-next-app@latest audition-invoice-tracker-voice-actors-narrators --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"
   ```

2. **Install dependencies:**
   ```
   npm install prisma @prisma/client next-auth @auth/prisma-adapter stripe resend recharts zod react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers date-fns
   npm install -D @types/node
   ```

3. **Install shadcn/ui and add components:**
   ```
   npx shadcn@latest init
   npx shadcn@latest add button input label select table dialog badge card tabs form calendar popover dropdown-menu separator skeleton toast
   ```

4. **Set up Prisma schema** (`prisma/schema.prisma`). Define these models:
   - `User` (id, email, name, image, emailVerified, stripeCustomerId, stripePriceId, stripeSubscriptionId, subscriptionStatus, trialEndsAt, createdAt)
   - `Account`, `Session`, `VerificationToken` (NextAuth standard)
   - `Audition` (id, userId, title, author, wordCount, finishedHours, clientName, submittedAt, status [enum: SUBMITTED/AWAITING/BOOKED/PASSED/EXPIRED], rightsType [enum: BUYOUT/ROYALTY_SHARE/UNION_RESIDUAL], notes, createdAt, updatedAt)
   - `Booking` (id, userId, auditionId [FK nullable], title, rightsType, agreedRate, rateType [enum: FLAT/PFH], finishedHours, exclusivityStart, exclusivityEnd, deliveryDeadline, status [enum: IN_PRODUCTION/DELIVERED/PAYMENT_PENDING/PAID/DISPUTE], createdAt, updatedAt)
   - `Invoice` (id, userId, bookingId [FK nullable], clientName, amount, dueDate, status [enum: DRAFT/SENT/PAID/OVERDUE], notes, createdAt, updatedAt)
   - `Payment` (id, userId, invoiceId [FK], amount, paidAt, method [enum: ACX_DIRECT/PAYPAL/CHECK/BANK_TRANSFER/OTHER], notes)
   - `RoyaltyShareProject` (id, userId, bookingId [FK nullable], title, finishedHours, royaltySplitPercent, acxRetailPrice, estimatedMonthlySales, buyoutEquivalentRate, createdAt, updatedAt)
   - `RateEntry` (id, userId, clientName, rightsType, ratePerFinishedHour, recordedAt, notes)
   ```
   npx prisma init
   npx prisma generate
   npx prisma db push
   ```

5. **Configure NextAuth v5** (`src/auth.ts`):
   - Google OAuth provider + Prisma adapter
   - Callbacks: add `subscriptionStatus` and `trialEndsAt` to session token from User record
   - Export `auth`, `signIn`, `signOut` handlers
   - Create `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`

6. **Set up environment variables** (`.env.local`):
   ```
   DATABASE_URL=
   NEXTAUTH_SECRET=
   NEXTAUTH_URL=
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
   GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=
   STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
   STRIPE_STARTER_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID=
   STRIPE_STARTER_YEARLY_PRICE_ID=
   STRIPE_PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE_ID=
   STRIPE_PRO_YEARLY_PRICE_ID=
   RESEND_API_KEY=
   RESEND_FROM_EMAIL=hello@narratrack.com
   ```

7. **Build the protected dashboard layout** (`src/app/dashboard/layout.tsx`):
   - Server component that calls `auth()` and redirects unauthenticated users to `/login`
   - Sidebar nav with links: Dashboard, Auditions, Bookings, Invoices & Payments, Royalty-Share ROI, Rate History, Settings
   - Responsive: sidebar collapses to hamburger on mobile

8. **Build the Audition module** (`src/app/dashboard/auditions/`):
   - `page.tsx`: server component fetching auditions via Prisma for the current user; renders `AuditionsTable` client component
   - `AuditionsTable`: shadcn DataTable with columns (title, author, submitted date, status badge, rights type, actions); filter controls for status and date range
   - `AddAuditionDialog`: controlled Dialog with react-hook-form + zod schema; POST to `/api/auditions` server action
   - `EditAuditionDialog`: same form, pre-populated; PATCH to `/api/auditions/[id]`
   - "Convert to Booking" button in row actions: opens `CreateBookingFromAuditionDialog` with audition data pre-filled
   - Server actions in `src/app/actions/auditions.ts`

9. **Build the Booking module** (`src/app/dashboard/bookings/`):
   - Same DataTable pattern; columns: title, rights type, rate, finished hours, exclusivity end date (highlighted red if within 30 days), status badge, actions
   - `AddBookingDialog` and `EditBookingDialog` with all booking fields
   - Booking detail page (`/dashboard/bookings/[id]`): full project view, linked audition, linked invoices

10. **Build the Invoice & Payment module** (`src/app/dashboard/invoices/`):
    - Invoice list with DataTable; columns: client, amount, due date, status badge, outstanding amount
    - `AddInvoiceDialog`: form fields + optional booking linkage
    - Invoice detail page (`/dashboard/invoices/[id]`): shows payment history, "Log Payment" button opens `LogPaymentDialog`
    - Overdue detection: server-side cron-compatible function that sets status to OVERDUE where dueDate < now and status = SENT

11. **Build the Dashboard page** (`src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`):
    - Server component; parallel Prisma queries for: active audition count, 30-day conversion rate, total outstanding invoices, next exclusivity window expiry, total payments received (current month)
    - Stat card components (shadcn Card) for each metric
    - `RateHistoryChart` client component using Recharts LineChart; data fetched server-side and passed as props

12. **Build the Royalty-Share ROI module** (Pro only) (`src/app/dashboard/royalty-share/`):
    - Gate: check `session.user.subscriptionStatus === 'active' && session.user.stripePriceId` includes Pro price IDs; redirect to `/pricing` if not
    - `RoyaltyShareCalculator`: client component with inputs (finished hours, royalty split %, ACX retail price, estimated monthly sales); computes breakeven month, 12/24-month projected earnings, buyout equivalent
    - Project list: saved RoyaltyShareProject records with comparison table (royalty-share projected vs. buyout equivalent)
    - Calculation logic in `src/lib/royalty-calculations.ts`

13. **Build the public Royalty-Share Calculator** (`src/app/royalty-share-calculator/page.tsx`):
    - No auth required, fully public
    - Same calculator component as in the dashboard but without save functionality
    - CTA at bottom: "Save your calculations and track all your ACX projects — free 14-day trial"
    - This is the primary SEO lead magnet page

14. **Set up Stripe** (`src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts`):
    - Webhook handler: listen for `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.payment_failed`
    - On each event, update User record: `stripeSubscriptionId`, `stripePriceId`, `subscriptionStatus`, `trialEndsAt`
    - Checkout session creation: server action `createCheckoutSession(priceId)` in `src/app/actions/billing.ts` — creates Stripe Checkout session with 14-day trial, redirects to success URL
    - Billing portal: server action `createBillingPortalSession()` for self-serve plan management
    - Pricing page (`src/app/pricing/page.tsx`): two-column card layout (Starter / Pro), monthly/yearly toggle, "Start free trial" button calls `createCheckoutSession`

15. **Set up Resend email** (`src/lib/email.ts`):
    - `sendWelcomeEmail(user)`: triggered on first login (NextAuth `signIn` event)
    - `sendOverdueInvoiceReminder(user, invoice)`: called by a daily cron-compatible API route (`/api/cron/check-overdue`)
    - `sendExclusivityWindowAlert(user, booking)`: called by `/api/cron/check-exclusivity` for bookings with `exclusivityEnd` within 7 days
    - `sendTrialEndingReminder(user)`: called by `/api/cron/check-trials` for users with `trialEndsAt` within 2 days
    - All cron routes protected by a `CRON_SECRET` header check; schedule with Coolify cron or an external cron service

16. **Build CSV export** (`src/app/api/export/[type]/route.ts`):
    - Route params: `type` = `auditions` | `bookings` | `payments`
    - Auth-protected server route; queries Prisma for current user's records; returns CSV with appropriate headers and `Content-Disposition: attachment`

17. **Build public marketing pages**:
    - `src/app/page.tsx`: homepage with hero ("Replace your ACX narrator spreadsheet"), feature overview, social proof section (leave placeholder for testimonials), CTA to free trial
    - `src/app/pricing/page.tsx`: pricing cards
    - `src/app/vs/spreadsheets/page.tsx`: comparison page targeting "acx narrator spreadsheet template" keyword
    - `src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`: MDX-powered blog posts (install `next-mdx-remote`); SEO meta tags via Next.js `generateMetadata`

18. **Configure SEO metadata** (`src/app/layout.tsx`):
    - Default `metadata` object with site name, description, OpenGraph tags
    - Per-page `generateMetadata` in landing pages and blog posts
    - `src/app/sitemap.ts`: generate sitemap including all blog post slugs and public pages
    - `src/app/robots.ts`: allow all, point to sitemap

19. **Verify build and containerize**:
    - Run `npm run build` — fix any type errors or missing env var references
    - Add to `next.config.ts`: `output: 'standalone'`
    - Create `Dockerfile`:
      ```
      FROM node:20-alpine AS base
      # ... standard Next.js standalone Dockerfile pattern
      # Copy .next/standalone, .next/static, public
      # EXPOSE 3000
      # CMD ["node", "server.js"]
      ```
    - Create `docker-compose.yml` with `web` and `postgres` services for local dev
    - Deploy to Coolify: connect repo, set environment variables, configure PostgreSQL service, set domain, enable SSL

20. **Post-deploy checklist before launch**:
    - Verify Stripe webhook endpoint is registered and receiving events in Stripe dashboard
    - Verify Google OAuth redirect URIs include production domain
    - Verify Resend domain is verified and sending
    - Test full signup → trial → calculator → Stripe checkout → paid subscriber flow end-to-end
    - Set up Plausible Analytics or Vercel Analytics on public pages
    - Verify `/royalty-share-calculator` is publicly accessible without auth and loads fast (it is the launch lead magnet)
